title: Heterogeneous-Goal Bayesian Adaptation for MAPE-K AI Workflows
research_question: Can Bayesian model averaging over multiple candidate system models improve adaptation quality in MAPE-K-style AI workflows when the controller must satisfy heterogeneous goals such as hard thresholds and optimization objectives simultaneously?
hypothesis: Extending Bayesian model averaging from single-goal self-adaptive systems to heterogeneous-goal AI workflows will reduce overconfident model selection, yielding better adaptation decisions and more stable performance under runtime uncertainty than single-model controllers.
motivation: The knowledge base highlights an explicit open problem: prior work on Bayesian model averaging for self-adaptive systems plans to extend to heterogeneous requirements such as threshold and optimization goals, but this gap remains unaddressed. This is attractive because it is grounded in a concrete future-work statement, fits the tracked self-adaptive-systems direction, and avoids recently rejected agentic-workflow ideas that focused on scheduling, routing, or decomposition. A successful result would provide a more robust adaptation mechanism for AI systems facing runtime uncertainty and conflicting objectives.
